{{nihongo|'''Zōsui'''|雑炊||literally "miscellaneous cooking"}}, or {{nihongo|'''ojiya'''|おじや|}}, is a mild and thin [[Japan]]ese [[rice]] [[soup]] akin to a rice-based [[vegetable soup]]. It is made from pre-cooked [[rice]] and dashi or water seasoned with either soy sauce or miso and cooked with other ingredients such as meat, seafood, mushrooms, and vegetables.<ref name="UI">{{cite web |title=Comfort Food Spotlight: Okayu and Zosui |url=https://www.umami-insider.com/comfort-food-spotlight-okayu-zosui/ |publisher=Umami Insider |access-date=5 November 2020 |archive-date=10 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201110162845/https://www.umami-insider.com/comfort-food-spotlight-okayu-zosui/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is generally served to those who are sick or otherwise feeling unwell, and is usually only served in the winter.

Leftover soup from [[Nabemono|nabe]] is often re-used for zosui. Instead of rice, [[udon]] and [[ramen]] noodles are recent alternatives.
